verdict_note: From reading only (no build, no tests run by the reviewer). Width is real. The 39 document types, the 10 doctypes (SHA-256 pinned), the MIME map, the library table, the 20 value types, the 14 control types, the 15 units, the curated CSS rows, the four transition lists and the 69-key script record match Master Spec v02.229 where spot-checked row by row. The 20 rows dispatch through one guarded arm, every edit goes through the host's existing SourcePatch, history and CommandContext path, and each refusal changes nothing. The strict authored-tree parser keeps format gaps whitespace-only (every byte belongs to a node, and </image> and </> are Unsupported nodes), so the formatter cannot delete markup bytes. The defects are in the edit semantics and in bounded work. F1 (high): web.remove_comment and web.apply_comment change content beyond the selection. Unwrapping a comment that holds an opening marker comments out the following markup or rules. The script tokenizer has no line-comment handling, so it can unwrap a string literal. A CSS or script comment applied inside an existing comment closes early. F2 (high): several hostile 8 MiB documents stall synchronous commands for minutes with no cancellation. Each CSS escape revalidates the whole rest of the buffer as UTF-8, balance-braces rescans the bracket stack quadratically, and indent, lint and validate have quadratic or allocation-heavy paths. F3 to F9 (medium): the formatter inserts visible spaces next to inline-level replaced elements. A trailing backslash in a css_rule value swallows the next declaration. Prefix reversal refuses to remove a hand-written transition. Rule identity decodes escapes, so distinct selectors collide, and edits land on the first of duplicate rules. html_all raises Error on valid head-less documents. Regions ignore the document type. The CC BY 4.0 attribution lacks the licence notice, and one 'WHATWG' attribute is not WHATWG. F10 to F14 are low. Licence: no copyleft source or table found; the data is consistent with the WHATWG standard text (input types in table order, global attributes in section order), but attribution is incomplete (F9). The pins (42 and the 18-row mutating list) are literal and correct at b57c82d1. The dispatch line conflicts textually, not semantically, with SMB-WEB-SITE-2 (rebase_note).

findings.certainty: READ (formatting.rs token walks; HTML comment end at the first '-->' and CSS comments do not nest, HTML Standard 13.2.5.43-.51 and CSS Syntax 3 4.3.2, not re-fetched); not run
findings.severity: high (a successful comment command silently comments out, or changes, content outside the selection; plain input, not hostile)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/formatting.rs:371-375 (html_comment unwrap keeps the inner text verbatim), :376-403 (css/javascript walk: the quote arm at :383-389 has no line-comment, regex or template-expression case; the /* arm at :390-397), :318-348 (comment_edit: the nest check at :334 tests only the selected text; for css/javascript there is no check that range.start and range.end lie outside an existing comment or string), :329-332 (an RCDATA title or textarea body is region 'html', so an HTML comment is applied there); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_code.rs:412-423
findings.what: (a) Unwrapping exposes markers. The HTML comment '<!-- a <!-- b -->' ends at the first '-->'. remove_comment replaces it with ' a <!-- b ', so a new comment opens there and runs to the next '-->' in the document, and every element in between leaves the DOM. CSS is the same: '/* a /* b */' unwraps to ' a /* b ', which comments out the following rules up to the next '*/'. The re-parse accepts both, so the command reports success. (b) In script, a quote inside a // comment ("// don't") opens a string in the walker. A later '/* x */' inside a real string literal is then taken as a comment and unwrapped, changing the string's value. (c) apply_comment on a CSS or script range inside an existing block comment gives '/* a /*b*/ c */'. The inner close ends the outer comment, so ' c */' becomes live CSS or script: a parse error that drops the following rule or breaks the script. A range across a // line end gives '// /*a' + newline + 'b*/', and 'b*/' is live code. A range inside a string inserts the markers into the string. (d) apply_comment inside <title> or <textarea> writes a literal '<!--x-->' into RCDATA text, which shows as visible text and is no comment.
findings.scenario:
(a) Source '

keep

'. web.remove_comment {offset: 5} reports scheme html_comment. The new DOM has no

, and 'keep' is comment text. (b) ''. web.remove_comment at the x gives var t = ' x '. (c) '' with web.apply_comment over 'b': the sheet now reads ' c */ p{top:0}', and the p rule is lost in error recovery.
findings.fix: Refuse instead of rewriting. Before unwrapping, refuse 'comment_inner_has_markers' when the inner text contains '<!--', '-->', '--!>' or ends with '<!-' (HTML), or contains '/*' (CSS and script). For apply in CSS and script, walk the region with one shared tokenizer that knows comments, strings, line comments and template literals (the bracket_pairs walker at hints.rs:429 already handles // ), and refuse 'range_splits_a_token' when either end is inside a comment, string or line comment. Use the same walker for remove. Refuse apply inside RCDATA bodies ('range_in_rcdata'), or state it as a cut.
findings.test: code_formatting.rs: (a) the nested-open HTML comment and the nested-open CSS comment each refuse with no change. (b) The // don't fixture refuses no_comment_here or unwraps only the real comment, and the string bytes are unchanged. (c) apply inside an existing /* */ and inside a string refuses. (d) apply inside <title> refuses. Each case adds no undo step through the harness 'refused' helper.

findings.certainty: READ (cost per call site); not run; seconds are estimates from operation counts
findings.severity: high (V4-02: a hostile document under the 8 MiB parse limit holds a synchronous web.* command for minutes, and the engine calls take no CancellationToken)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/css_properties.rs:846 (decode_escape: std::str::from_utf8(b.get(j..)) validates the WHOLE rest of the buffer for every non-hex escape), called from :807 (at_keyword, with b = the whole document via :786 scan_level and :824 media_query_text) and :876 (normalised, per rule prelude: :1163, :1329, :1437); crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/hints.rs:463 (bracket_pairs: rposition scans the whole stack for every closer with no opener); crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/formatting.rs:441-450 (indent_edits: for each verbatim element, starts.iter().any over every line start) and :451-467 (one TextEdit and String per line before coalesce); crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/validation.rs:691 with vocabulary.rs:425-441 (attribute() clones the whole merged attribute list, about 54 definitions, for every attribute of every element), :1050-1064 (seen.contains per attribute), :1153-1170 (duplicate-properties and vendor-prefix are O(d^2) per rule, d up to 8192); crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/css_properties.rs:1337-1369 (rule_edit re-scans the block once per change and once per removed duplicate); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_code.rs:252-459 (no engine call takes cancel; only patched() does)
findings.what:
The lane's hostile tests cover nesting depth and the regex engine. They do not cover these paths. (1) '. Every at-rule runs up to 33 full-document UTF-8 validations, about 8192 x 33 x 8 MiB = 2e12 bytes, which is minutes. web.media_records, web.css_rule, web.code_navigator and web.lint css all scan. One 4 MiB selector made of escaped letters is O(n^2) in normalised. (2) A script of 4M '(' then 4M '}' makes web.balance_braces cost about 1.6e13 steps. (3) 100k empty 
 plus 7 MB of newlines makes web.indent over the whole document cost about 7e11, and allocates millions of TextEdits first. (4) 2.7M distinct attributes make web.validate do roughly 350M allocations. (5) 256 rules of 8192 prefixed declarations make web.lint css do about 8e9 string comparisons. None of these refuse typed or can be canceled, and jobs: none is declared.
findings.scenario: A model opens a downloaded page (under 8 MiB, parses fine) and calls web.lint {language: css}. The drive's JSONL loop blocks for minutes, and the host cannot cancel because the engine never checks the token.
findings.fix: decode_escape decodes one char from at most four bytes (text.get(j..).and_then(|s| s.chars().next()) on a &str, or from_utf8 over b[j..min(j+4,len)]). bracket_pairs keeps one stack per bracket kind, or treats a closer whose kind is not on top as unmatched in O(1). indent_edits binary-searches the sorted line starts per verbatim span and refuses over a line budget (for example 65536 lines, 'range_too_large'). validate looks up attributes by reference without cloning (a find over tag.attributes, then the groups). lint keeps a HashSet per element or rule. rule_edit applies all changes in one declarations() pass. Pass the CancellationToken into lint, validate, rule_edit, format_edits and indent_edits and check it per element or per item. Add a work budget with a typed 'work_budget_exceeded' refusal, or admit these rows through the JobPort (Q1).
findings.test: Five hostile fixtures, each just under Limits::default().max_bytes: escapes in at-keywords and in one selector, unmatched closers in a script, verbatim elements with many lines, many attributes, and many prefixed declarations. Each command returns or refuses typed within a stated bound (for example 2 s on the round machine). A pre-canceled token refuses 'canceled' with no change.

Whitespace is inserted where none existed, next to inline-level content. '

findings.certainty: READ; CSS Syntax 3 4.3.8 (a backslash followed by a non-newline is a valid escape)
findings.severity: medium (one call silently invalidates a neighbouring declaration while reporting success)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/css_properties.rs:1187-1223 (checked_css_text: '\\' skips two bytes at :1202, so a value ENDING in a backslash passes), :1342 (replace_range of the value before the existing ';'), :1345 and :1351 (appended 'prop: v;')
findings.what: Take the value 'red' + backslash (JSON "red\\"). It has no control character, no '</', no comment markers and no top-level ';', '{' or '}', so it is accepted. Written as 'color: red' + backslash + ';', the backslash escapes the semicolon. The declaration then runs on into the next one ('margin: 0;'), and the parser drops both. In the one-line form the following '}' is not escaped, but the next declaration of an existing block is lost.
findings.scenario: Rule '.a { color: red; margin: 0; }'. web.css_rule {stylesheet, selector: '.a', declarations: {color: 'blue' + backslash}} succeeds, and margin no longer applies.
findings.fix: In checked_css_text, refuse a value, selector or media text whose last code point is a backslash, or whose backslash is followed by a newline ('css_value_invalid'). Better: tokenize the text with the sheet tokenizer and require that it ends at a token boundary outside any escape.
findings.test: rule_edit_refuse_text: a value ending in a backslash refuses css_value_invalid, and the existing margin declaration's bytes are unchanged.

findings.certainty: READ against STU-WEB-072 ('removing the base declaration removes its emitted prefixes in the same edit')
findings.severity: medium (a hand-written or imported transition cannot be removed through the command)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/css_properties.rs:1295-1300 (removal expands to -webkit-transition, -o-transition and transition), :1355-1359 (each expanded removal refuses css_property_absent when that property is not in the block); :1295 (a per-value rule matches on c.value, which is None for a removal, so a value rule's emissions are never removed)
findings.what: STU-WEB-072's delete sentinel removes the emissions when the base is removed. Here the emissions are mandatory. 'a { transition: opacity 1s }' was written without prefixes, by hand or by another tool, so declarations {transition: null} refuses css_property_absent on -webkit-transition, and the base cannot be removed at all. The shipped rule has value None, so the per-value case is latent, but a registered per-value rule could never be reversed. The only removal test (an_existing_rule_is_changed_in_place_and_removal_takes_the_emitted_prefixes) starts from a block the edit itself wrote.
findings.scenario: Open a page whose sheet has 'nav a { transition: color .2s }' and remove transition: refused css_property_absent. A model concludes the property is absent, though it is there.
findings.fix: Treat emitted properties as optional on removal: remove those present, refuse only when the BASE is absent, and list in 'removed' only what was removed. For per-value rules, read the base's current value from the block to pick the rule whose emissions to remove.
findings.test: A block with transition only: removal succeeds, removed == ['transition'], and every other byte is unchanged. A block with -webkit-transition and transition but no -o-transition removes the two present.

findings.certainty: READ; the base-10 specificity is pre-existing css.rs, newly surfaced by web.code_navigator
findings.severity: medium (an edit can land on the wrong rule or have no effect, while it reports set)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/css_properties.rs:854-892 (normalised decodes escapes), :1305 and :1329 (rule identity = normalised text equality, and find() takes the FIRST rule with that selector), :1341-1342 (replacing the value drops an existing !important), :1380-1397 (a new top-level rule is appended at the END of the sheet, after every @media block), :1437-1438 (code navigator: normalised then crate::css::parse_selectors, which splits on ',' after the escapes are decoded); crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/css.rs:287-293 (specificity = ids*100 + classes*10 + tag)
findings.what: (1) Escape decoding makes distinct selectors equal. '.a' + backslash + ',b' (one class named 'a,b') and '.a,b' (a list) both normalise to '.a,b'. web.css_rule {selector: '.a,b'} therefore edits the single-class rule, and the code navigator reports that rule as matching any element of class 'a'. The same holds for an escaped '.'. (2) Spacing and case differences ('a>b' against 'a > b', 'DIV' against 'div') create a duplicate rule instead of editing the existing one. (3) With two '.a' rules, the first is edited, while the later one wins the cascade, so the edit has no visible effect. (4) A new top-level '.a' is appended after '@media (max-width:600px) { .a {...} }', so it overrides the responsive rule at every width. (5) Setting color on 'color: red !important' writes 'color: blue' and silently drops !important. (6) Specificity is reported base-10: 10 classes outrank one id.
findings.scenario: Sheet '@media (max-width:600px){ .card{padding:0} }'. web.css_rule {selector: '.card', declarations: {padding: '24px'}} appends '.card{padding:24px}' at the end, and phones now get 24px.
findings.fix: Compare selectors on a token sequence that keeps escapes escaped (normalise whitespace around combinators, lowercase only type selectors), not on decoded text. Edit the LAST same-selector rule at the level, or refuse 'css_rule_ambiguous' with the candidates. Insert a new top-level rule before the first @media block of the sheet, or report 'overrides_media_rules' (Q5). Keep !important unless the value says otherwise, or state the reading. Report specificity as the (a,b,c) triple. Do not split a selector list on a decoded comma.
findings.test: One test per item: the escaped-comma selector is not the list; 'a>b' edits 'a > b'; the duplicate-rule case; the new rule lands before @media (or the report flag); !important kept; specificity [0,10,0] < [1,0,0].

findings.certainty: READ (validation.rs context rule; acceptance of head-less documents read from dom/construction.rs docs N1, not run)
findings.severity: medium (Error-severity diagnostics on valid HTML; a model 'fixing' them rewrites correct pages)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/validation.rs:603-606 (head and body require parent html; title and base require parent head), :716-731 (the parent is the AUTHORED parent; the document root has no local name, so ok is false); crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/dom.rs:24-27 (N1: implied html, head and body are accepted, not refused)
findings.what:
't

x

' is valid HTML, and the parser accepts it with title as a child of the document root. web.validate reports tag_context_violation (Error) 'title is not legal inside <>'. The same happens for base, and for head or body when is omitted. The tests always author html and head.
findings.scenario: web.validate on any minimal page without <head> reports one or more errors, and web.lint doctype-first passes on the same page.
findings.fix: In the context check, treat the N1 implied skeleton as present. A parent that is the document root or an authored html satisfies 'head' for head-content elements and 'html' for head and body. Or skip context rules whose required parent is an implied-capable element (html, head, body, tbody, colgroup) when that element is not authored.

findings.certainty: READ against STU-WEB-029, -046, -047, -050; JavaScript MIME essence list per WHATWG MIME Sniffing (not re-fetched)
findings.severity: medium (wrong language at the cursor in two common cases; the hint record is short of the spec's shape)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/hints.rs:190-234 (regions treat every document as HTML; the document type is not an input), :237-239 (region_at: an offset equal to an embedded block's end belongs to the next html region), :134-155 (register checks ambiguity only within one scheme; registered schemes' delimiters are never used by regions()), :174-179 (script_scheme lists 6 of the JavaScript MIME essences), :252-259 and :331-340 (HintContext drops additional_dismiss_chars, allow_whitespace_prefix and display_restriction); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_code.rs:233-239 (code_type picks css or javascript by file name), :347 (hint JSON)
findings.what: (1) web.open accepts a .css or .js file, and code_type then reads css or javascript, but regions() returns one html region. web.apply_comment writes '<!-- -->', which CSS ignores (CDO and CDC at the top level), so the rule stays live. In a script it is a syntax error or a legacy HTML-like comment. code_hints answers html groups or none. (2) The usual typing position, the cursor right before </style> or </script>, resolves to html, so code_hints gives no CSS hint there, and uncomment of a comment ending at the block end answers no_comment_here. (3) The registration diagnoses only same-scheme duplicates. Two schemes opening on '<?php' for overlapping types are not diagnosed (STU-WEB-046), and a registered scheme never owns a region (STU-WEB-027 'on equal terms'). (4) type='text/x-javascript', 'application/x-ecmascript', 'text/livescript' and 'text/javascript1.x' run as script in browsers but are treated as text here. (5) The web.code_hints hint omits three of the six STU-WEB-050 fields that the engine record has.
findings.scenario: Open styles.css (text 'p{color:red}'), then web.apply_comment {start: 0, end: 12}: success, scheme html, file '<!--p{color:red}-->', and the rule still applies in a browser.
findings.fix: Make regions() take the document type. TEXT kinds css, less, scss and sass are one css region, javascript and json one javascript region, text one text region. For an embedded block, let an offset equal to its end resolve to the block for hints and remove. Diagnose cross-scheme duplicate opening delimiters for overlapping applies_to_document_types, and either use registered delimiters in regions() or state that registration is record-only. Complete the JavaScript MIME essence list. Emit the three missing hint fields.
findings.test: A .css document: apply_comment uses /* */, and code_hints gives css groups. The offset at '</style>' with 'p{col' before it gives css_properties with prefix 'col'. Two schemes on '<?php' for 'php' refuse delimiter_ambiguous. type='text/x-javascript' gives a javascript region. The hint JSON carries the six fields.

findings.certainty: READ the data and notices; the WHATWG notice and the attribute index were fetched 2026-11-13 (index: no 'controlslist' row between 'controls' and 'coords'; 'color' on link present); no GPL, LGPL or MPL source read
findings.severity: medium (licence compliance: CC BY 4.0 is claimed but its attribution conditions are not met; a provenance claim is inaccurate)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/vocabulary.rs:5-14 and crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/validation.rs:6-7 (the only attribution: 'WHATWG HTML Living Standard ... (CC BY 4.0, recorded in builders/dep-requests.jsonl)'; no URL, copyright notice, licence link, snapshot date or change note); no NOTICE in crates/hsk-studio-web-core or crates/hsk-studio-web (precedent: crates/hsk-studio-layout/NOTICE and LICENSES-W3C); vocabulary.rs:638 ('controlslist' in MEDIA_FLAGS, which is not in the WHATWG attribute index: a WICG/Chromium attribute), :631 (the referrerpolicy tokens come from the W3C Referrer Policy spec); hints.rs:64 ('ECMA-262 12.7.2') against the dep line's '13.x' and its single license 'CC-BY-4.0'; S/tools/license_gate.py OK set has no CC-BY-4.0; S/tools/license_evidence.json asset_licenses has no entry
findings.what: Verdict on the source: no sign of copying from a copyleft project. The element names, the input types in the standard's own table order, the global attributes in the standard's section order and the content-model contexts are what the WHATWG text states. No descriptions were shipped (every hint group is described=false), so no MDN (CC BY-SA) prose came in. Names and enumerations are largely facts. But the builder chose CC BY 4.0, and its Section 3(a) attribution is not given: the notice 'Copyright (c) WHATWG (Apple, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft)', the licence name with its URI, the source URI and date, and an indication of changes (Studio-declared formatting classes, a subset). The data ships in a crate with no NOTICE. The claim 'the attributes and enumerated values that standard defines' is false for controlslist and for the referrerpolicy tokens. The ECMA-262 reserved words are under Ecma's copyright notice, not CC BY. The HTMLHint, CSSLint and JSHint rule names come from the spec's lists (facts; their projects are MIT) and need no notice.
findings.scenario: A distribution audit of the product binaries finds WHATWG-derived tables with no CC BY 4.0 notice. The round's licence gate does not see data lines at all.
findings.fix: Add crates/hsk-studio-web-core/NOTICE in the hsk-studio-layout shape. Name the HTML Standard (Living Standard, snapshot date such as 'Last Updated 12 November 2026'), https://html.spec.whatwg.org/, the notice 'Copyright (c) WHATWG (Apple, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft)', CC BY 4.0 with https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, and the changes (subset, Studio formatting classes, Studio-authored rule set). Name the Referrer Policy (W3C) and ECMA-262 sources separately with their own notices. Remove controlslist, or move it to a 'non-standard' list with its source. Split the dep-requests line per source with its own licence. Record an asset_licenses entry for the steward (Q3).
findings.test: None in code. The steward's asset_licenses verification: NOTICE present and complete, each data source named with its licence, controlslist absent or attributed.

findings.certainty: READ (no BOM handling anywhere in web-core dom.rs or web_commands.rs open and save)
findings.severity: low (encoding and prolog placement on the doctype insert path; a claim larger than the code)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/formatting.rs:488 (insert at 0..0); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_commands.rs:426 (from_utf8 keeps U+FEFF as text), :562-589 (save writes the bytes as-is and never reads writes_byte_order_mark); lane capabilities_done 'STU-WEB-011..016'
findings.what: With a document that starts with a UTF-8 BOM and has no doctype, web.set_doctype inserts the declaration BEFORE the BOM. The file no longer starts with a BOM, so a browser opening it without a charset declaration falls back to a legacy encoding. The U+FEFF becomes a body character. An XHTML document starting with '<?xml ...?>' gets the doctype before the XML declaration, which must come first. The four BOM-writing types of STU-WEB-013 are data only: save never writes a BOM. The lane lists the per-document override as cut, but not the default write.
findings.scenario:
'\uFEFF

caf\u00e9

' saved after set_doctype html_5 begins '' and then U+FEFF. Opened from disk without a meta charset, 'cafe' with an accent renders as mojibake.
findings.fix: Insert after a leading U+FEFF and after a leading XML declaration (a root-level Unsupported processing-instruction node). Name 'save does not apply writes_byte_order_mark' as a cut, or apply it when the type is known.
findings.test: A BOM fixture: set_doctype keeps the BOM at byte 0. An '<?xml?>' fixture: the doctype follows the declaration.

findings.severity: low (STU-WEB-028 'dry-runnable (returns the diff)': the diff can be silently partial)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_code.rs:161-163 (edits_json: replacement cut to 512 characters by row_text, no flag), :405-409; crates/hsk-studio-web-core/src/formatting.rs:248-267 (coalesce merges edits and their unchanged bytes into chunks of any size)
findings.what: Past 1024 edits the edits are coalesced, so one diff entry can span kilobytes of the document. The dry-run reply truncates every replacement at 512 characters and sets no 'truncated' flag. A model that previews or applies the returned diff works on a wrong one. sha256_after is the only check.
findings.scenario: web.format_source {dry_run: true} on a 3000-item list: about 1024 entries, each truncated without notice.

answers.licence: Clean source, incomplete attribution. No GPL, LGPL or MPL project or table was used, as far as the data shows: the HTML element and attribute names and enumerations follow the WHATWG text and its order, no prose descriptions shipped, and the vendor counts are not reproduced. Attribution exists only as a doc-comment mention. There is no CC BY 4.0 notice, licence URI, source URI or date, change note, crate NOTICE or asset_licenses entry, and license_gate.py does not list CC-BY-4.0. controlslist is not WHATWG, referrerpolicy tokens are W3C, and the ECMA-262 words are Ecma copyright (F9). The dep-requests line exists (last line of builders/dep-requests.jsonl) but conflates three sources under one licence.
answers.formatter_round_trip: No byte loss: the strict authored-tree parser makes every format gap whitespace from text nodes only (every byte belongs to a node; </image> and </> are Unsupported nodes). Verbatim: pre, script, style and textarea, plus RAWTEXT, RCDATA and foreign content (CDATA sections are foreign Unsupported nodes) are untouched. CRLF follows the document's first line ending, and other endings are normalised only inside rewritten gaps. Idempotent by construction (same gaps, same targets) and tested on one fixture. The undo step is one named step ('Format Source') through WebHost::edit, with an exact inverse from patched(). Defects: visible whitespace next to inline-level elements (F3), comment edits (F1), BOM and prolog on the doctype insert (F10), the partial dry-run diff (F11), and large documents bounded by 1024 coalesced edits but with transient memory on indent (F2).
answers.validator_and_linters: Typed diagnostics with severity, rule_set_id, rule_id, byte_range, element_path, message and code. Output capped at 2000 with a truncated count, never a rewrite. The script lint refuses typed (provider unselected), and rules that do not run are listed in not_run. The pattern engine is a genuine Pike VM: linear, bounded program size, refuses back-references, look-around and lazy quantifiers, no panics found. Work is not bounded on hostile input (F2). Implied-skeleton false errors (F7). Codes and configuration (F13).
answers.css_rule_edit: Tokenised scanning (comments, strings, escapes, nesting depth 16, item budget). One TextEdit for the rule block or the insertion. Untouched declarations are kept byte for byte, except the whitespace run before the end of the level, which is rewritten on insert (documented). @media is matched by parsed records, one level deep; nested media is not searched, @supports is opaque, and both are silently omitted from web.media_records and web.code_navigator rather than refused. Defects: F4 (trailing backslash), F5 (prefix reversal), F6 (identity, placement, !important, specificity), F2 (escape decode cost).
answers.regions_and_hints: Regions come from tokenizer spans, never patterns (STU-WEB-047 met for the shipped html scheme). Receipts carry range, candidates (winner only), decision, delimiters and enclosing owner. Hints: tag, attribute, enumerated value, CSS property and CSS value groups built from the vocabulary, described=false flagged. Defects in F8.
answers.host_integration: Typed refusals throughout (CodeError mapped to No with a byte range). Every mutating row is one WebHost history step labelled with the catalog row's display_name, with the caller's CommandContext (actor, client_session, command_id, correlation) checked by test. It survives web.save and web.open, and the run emits one observe frame per command (tests assert frames == 1). Controls descriptors come from RUN_COMMANDS through ui_seed (studio.command.web.*). JobPort: none of the 20 rows is admitted, and the engine calls ignore the CancellationToken. That matches jobs: none, but it is not acceptable with the F2 costs (Q1). The drive-session test is feature viewer, and .config/round-features.toml enables viewer for hsk-studio-harness (rule 4e met). The it3 focused harness run did not include it (12 tests, viewer off).
